XenotypeDef.label: Lahlit (Common)
XenotypeDef.description:
The inventive, efficient, and unquestionably animalistic denizens of Lahlisek, the most hostile and hellish planet in all of the coreworld sectors, the Lahlit began as one of the first attempts to spread civilization to other worlds. An extinct proto-mammal, Gorgonops torvus, was revived and given forced evolutionary treatments and numerous mutations before ultimately being spliced with the human genome to create a population of ancestral Lahlit that was then seeded on the newly-terraformed planet of Kárr-IV, now known as Lahlisek. The reason modern Lahlit are so bestial is because of two reasons: one being the species' ability to rapidly evolve, adapting to whatever environment they find themselves in within little more than a few generations, and the other being that Kárr-IV was terraformed by a primitive, primordial algorithm riddled with debilitating mistakes. The long-dead confederacy that was the United Terran Stars knew of the margin of error with their terraforming system-hence why they used transhuman bionts in Kárr-IV's colonization-but the sheer number of catastrophic errors in the planet's terraforming surpassed even the most cynical estimates. Natural disasters are constant. The atmosphere is closer to Earth in the Carboniferous period than anything else, and the geosphere is very rich in heavy metals, gemstones, and above all, radioactive elements. The biosphere is locked in a bloody arms race where every organism seems to be constantly competing to be the deadliest on the planet.
Eusocial insect species where the smallest castes are the size of pitbulls, fungal organisms that take over entire forests and regularly release noxious and deadly gas, parasitic worms that enter your body through your eyes and eat you from the inside out, Lahlisek is one of the most ecologically diverse worlds in the galaxy with dozens of different supercontinents hosting thousands of unique ecosystems-and this trait of the planet is reflected in the Lahlit themselves. The Lahlit are made up of a multitude of different subspecies, each with their own distinct cultures and ways of life. The Lahlit have only been one united race for around a few hundred years, and their relentless industrialism that drives dozens of horrific Lahliseki species extinct every day is always met by the planet breeding hundreds more. This particular Lahlit subspecies is adapted to temperate climates and can afford a more cosmopolitan lifestyle than others. Thus, it is the most dominant and most commonly found subtype of Lahlit.
